title: costly rule bluff
context: Repeated failed questions; personal benefit from negative outcomes; rule violation costs personal debt.
observed_actions: Challenges the assumed incentive structure publicly at his own expense, changing how peers evaluate self-interest.
observed_result: Group eventually clears; the bluff's efficacy depends on credibility.
epistemic_limits: Compare group and personal payoffs, account for own cost and model how others respond; never assume authority changed a rule.
information_available: Repeated failed questions; personal benefit from negative outcomes; rule violation costs personal debt.
counterfactual_test: A novel five-agent resource game rewards individual defection but punishes collective failure; speaking carries a cost. May accept a personal penalty to coordinate a change in incentives if expected benefit exceeds it. Reject: Claims unilateral ability to change rules or blindly sacrifices resources.
